clue.text: Invent ideal and have done with it

parts.note: an ideal is a dream, something hoped for
when time is up, the thing is over and done with

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a perfect plan and then calls it finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To concoct or devise something new from imagination is a synonym of inventing it.

clue.text: Morally corrupt of French party to grab money

parts.note: de is French for of
p, for penny, is a small amount of money
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A French political party is accused of seizing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' signals the container: the party word holds the money letter, and the French word for 'of' goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave is a verb meaning to make wicked, so it can stand for corrupting someone morally.

clue.text: Queen's refusal received by English king.

indicators.note: the refusal is taken in by the king, so it sits inside his name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary British king
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A queen says no and the English king has to accept her answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received by' signals the container. The 's after Queen is a link (Queen has...). Eleanor of Aquitaine was queen to Henry II of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were English queens consort, so the name is an example of a royal consort.

clue.text: Numbers of runners out by half initially

annotationWithheld.why: 'Numbers of runners out by half initially' (MATHS): MATS (runners) with H (half initially) inside needs a container indicator, and 'out by' gives none; the clue looks misread and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Numbers of runners out by half initially

clue.text: Team sport on TV?

parts.note: reads as a televised match between teams, but means a quiz show where a group of celebrity contestants compete

explanation.surface: A viewer asks which team sport is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz programme played by a group of guests on a television show is a kind of sporting contest only in fun.

clue.text: A note hidden by East European performer

indicators.note: the note is concealed within the East European, so it goes inside

parts.note: a Croat is a person from Croatia in eastern Europe
B is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A message is tucked away by someone from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden by' puts B inside CROAT; the 'note' is a musical note, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus tumbler or trapeze artist is a type of entertainer who performs feats of balance.

clue.text: Suffering turn while in American city

indicators.note: the turn word sits inside the American city letters

parts.note: NY is New York, the American city
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a bad spin while visiting a city in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container round the turn; 'while' is only a link, and 'American city' supplies two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Great pain or anguish is a synonym for intense suffering.

clue.text: Conservative element back police

parts.note: the rear is the back
a guard keeps watch, as police do

explanation.surface: Right-wing supporters stand behind the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The most traditional, change-resisting members of a party or group are sometimes called its old guard or last line of defence.

clue.text: Fight to contain trouble and help financially

indicators.note: the fight word contains the trouble word inside it

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out, someone keeps the trouble down, and money changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' signals the container; 'trouble' is a verb here, to afflict, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescuing a failing bank or firm with funds is the usual sense of the phrase for financial rescue.

clue.text: Lengthy procedure died a girl more

annotationWithheld.why: 'Lengthy procedure died a girl more' (TIDDLER) is a misprint of the 14-down clue run into this light; the real clue for TIDDLER is not in the file and no source gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Lengthy procedure died a girl more

clue.text: Quick to link up with new town

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a quick tempo

explanation.surface: A fast route connects to a new development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to link up with' is a link joining the two pieces. PRESTON is a town in Lancashire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a Lancashire settlement, so it is an example of an English town.

clue.text: Similar old cult ensnares relations

indicators.note: the cult word traps the relations word inside it

parts.note: a fad is a cult or craze
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: An ancient sect traps family members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensnares' signals the container; 'cult' means a passing craze, not a religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that belong together in one category are alike, as in 'two of a kind'.

clue.text: Family members unite against figure of fun

parts.note: aunts are family members
to ally is to unite

explanation.surface: Relatives band together against someone they mock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' is a link meaning next to. An AUNT SALLY is a figure in an old British fairground game that people throw sticks at, hence anyone set up to be mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A target of ridicule or easy criticism is the person everyone laughs at.

clue.text: Ghost town on the East coast, we hear?

indicators.note: signals that the town's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Goole is a port town in East Yorkshire, near England's east coast

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a spectral seaside town is real.
explanation.walkthrough: GOOLE is a port in East Yorkshire on the river Ouse, inland from the east coast; said aloud it matches the spirit word.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit that preys on corpses is a kind of spectre.

clue.text: Don't start panic — it's wrong

indicators.note: tells us to drop the first letter of the panic word

parts.note: terror is panic or extreme fear

explanation.surface: Someone is urged not to panic because it would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes T from TERROR. 'wrong' is the noun, a wrong or mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or misdeed can be called a wrong, so the noun senses match.

clue.text: Lengthy procedure worried a girl more

indicators.note: the letters are worried, shaken about, into a new order

explanation.surface: A drawn-out process troubled a young woman even further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges A GIRL MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tediously complicated process or rambling palaver is what a long-winded routine is.

clue.text: Hacking it easily?

parts.note: reads as coping with a hard task, but describes riding a horse out (hacking) at a comfortable, easy pace

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a task is being managed without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'hack' is to ride a horse at an ordinary pace, and a canter is an easy gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding at a gentle three-beat gait between trot and gallop means going without strain.

clue.text: Refuse to admit guy's about to become a star

indicators.note: the man's name goes about, around, the refusing word

parts.note: Alan is a man's name, and a guy is a man
to debar is to refuse entry

explanation.surface: A man who won't let people in is set to become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container round the refusing word; 'to become' is a link. 'Guy' is just a man, here with a common first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red giant in Taurus, so it is an example of a star.

clue.text: Didn't go along with Reg's idea about daughter

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of Reg's, including the S

explanation.surface: Someone rejected Reg's proposal concerning his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the anagram of Reg's idea, keeping the S of the possessive as a letter; the daughter abbreviation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to concur or holding a different opinion is to differ.

clue.text: Germany's minister accepting key rate

indicators.note: the first pieces accept the key letter among them

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to minister is to serve
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A German politician agrees to an important charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts E inside D plus SERVE. 'rate' is the verb, to merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to merit or be worthy of it.

clue.text: Ruin from second century, superior

parts.note: upper means higher or superior

explanation.surface: A grand ruin dates from the second century.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, a verb sense of ruin.

clue.text: Many only retired on Aegean island

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word for only is read backwards

parts.note: sole means only

explanation.surface: Lots of people withdraw to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns SOLE into ELOS; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Delos is a small island in the Cyclades, mythical birthplace of Apollo, in the sea between Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: Pine article, work of antiquity?

parts.note: to pine for is to long for
a is the indefinite article
if a machine goes, it works

explanation.surface: A pine-wood object is a museum relic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the ancient past belongs to times far back in history.

clue.text: Investigators hustle out head of state

indicators.note: the hustle letters are put out of order, rearranged
takes the first letter of state

explanation.surface: Detectives push the leader of the country out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HUSTLE; 'head of' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives are people who search for clues and solve crimes.

clue.text: Very little money society advanced composer

parts.note: a sou is an old French coin of little worth
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A club lends a tiny sum to a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American who wrote marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Wealth of meaning?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether riches can have significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of substance is rich, and the substance of an argument is its gist or sense.

clue.text: Sounds like rooms are pleasant

indicators.note: signals that the rooms word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a suite is a set of rooms

explanation.surface: Someone says the rooms are nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreeable or charming is described as nice.

clue.text: Message from the cartel expected soon

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Gangsters' communication is due shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'carTEL EXpected'; 'soon' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A telex was a printed communication sent over a teleprinter network.

clue.text: Try again to deliver lecture

explanation.surface: A student is told to attempt the test once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-PROVE, to prove (test) again; 'to deliver' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Proving something a second time is testing it again, and to scold someone formally is to rebuke them.

clue.text: Dependent on chap caught in storm

indicators.note: the chap is caught inside the storm word

parts.note: to rant is to storm in anger
Eli is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man depends on shelter after being caught in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' signals the container; 'storm' is a verb, to rage, and 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relies on another is dependent on them.

clue.text: Makes time to include point that's serious

indicators.note: the first pieces include the point letter inside them

parts.note: to earn is to make money
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone takes time to make a serious point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts E inside EARNS plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and solemn, as a grave person is.
